what: Agents in flight, and why. A finished agent is REMOVED from this file, not marked done — the page shows what is happening now, and history lives in git.

agents.what: What better ordering can buy, before anyone spends a week buying it
agents.why: Two steps lose forty-six of the sixty-six points, and both are the same thing: the order we put the funds in. Before we work on it, one question has to be answered. If the ordering were PERFECT — right fund first, every time it is anywhere on the list — what would the number be? That is the ceiling on every ordering effort we could ever run. It also asks where the right fund actually sits when we lose it: at rank nine, which a small improvement reaches, or at rank sixty, which no reshuffling of a forty-row list can.

agents.what: The ordering itself, and a term it does not contain
agents.why: We closed off this area months ago on a study that could not prove which ranking engine it ran on, and its conclusion was drawn from the wrong comparison. Re-run properly: single signals stay dead, but a blend of them beats what ships by a margin that clears its own error bars, and its biggest term is how near a fund is to the founder's own country — which our live scoring has no notion of. Graded at both places we cut the list, because a reshuffle can buy reach and no accuracy.

agents.what: Three more facts on each fund, and a leak the guard cannot see
agents.why: We hold about forty-six facts on every fund and show the AI eleven. An audit killed thirty-one of the thirty-five we withhold — too rare, or identical across every fund on the menu. Three survived and get one measured trial each. The more important half: a fourth field is tempting and is computed from who actually won money before, and our safeguard against the AI reading the answer key checks field NAMES, so it would not catch it. That safeguard gets taught to reason about where a number came from.
